chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Percussionists: Bilingue, Chino Pozo, Escollies and Tito Puente
summary: Machito sorts out the rhythm section: Escollies on timbales, Bilingue briefly, Chino Pozo on bongo, and Puente as timbalero and drummer.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Okay, then it was in 1944 when Carlos Vidal came into the orchestra.
Right.
Okay, Bilingue was with the band for about six months.
Less than that.
Less than that. Okay, who replaced Bilingue?
Chinito
Chino Pozo?
Chino Pozo and Tito Puente, because the original timbale player was Tony Escollies, you know, El Cojito.
I see, right.
... and Bilingue. That was the rhythm section. The bass was Andino and piano, Frank Ayala; and then Chinito - ahh - Chino---bongocero---- , Chino Pozo.

No more than two or three months.

Chino Pozo

in timbales

In and out he was about a year.
